note: We offer a small menu that changes daily. The chef requests that guests put their whole order in at once.
raw_note: An asterisk (*) marks dishes served raw or under-cooked. Flag the allergy/raw advisory when guests ask.

items.name: Sea Wolf Bakery Baguette
items.desc: les prés salés butter, sea salt
items.story: A baguette from Sea Wolf Bakers in Seattle's Fremont neighborhood, one of the Pacific Northwest's most celebrated naturally leavened bakeries. Baked the same day, served with Belgian-churned les prés salés butter flecked with coarse Camargue sea salt crystals. Simple and non-negotiable — this one never changes.

ingredients.note: Seattle's Fremont neighborhood bakery, founded 2014 by brothers Jesse and Kit Schumann. All breads are naturally leavened using Pacific Northwest grains. Named one of the 100 best bakeries in the U.S. by Food & Wine.

Belgian-churned cultured butter, 82% butterfat, finished with hand-harvested coarse sea salt crystals from the Camargue — a salt marsh region in the south of France. Richer and more complex than standard salted butter.
Flaky finishing salt from Essex, England. Prized for its pyramid-shaped crystals, clean flavor, and satisfying crunch.

items.name: Castelvetrano Olives
items.story: Meaty Nocellara del Belice olives from the Valle del Belice in southwestern Sicily — one of the only olive varieties with a Protected Designation of Origin. Marinated in-house with citrus peel, garlic, chili flake, and olive oil, then finished with a dusting of fennel pollen and rosemary. Bright, buttery, mild.

ingredients.note: Nocellara del Belice variety, named for the Sicilian town of Castelvetrano. PDO-protected, so they can only come from the Valle del Belice. Lye-cured for a clean, buttery flavor with no bitterness — the least aggressive olive on any table.
The fine yellow pollen harvested from wild fennel flowers. Intensely aromatic, floral, and anise-forward — used here as a finishing garnish.

items.allergenNote: Confirmed: the marinade carries garlic (allium) and chili flake. The garlic is marinated in, so it can't be picked out — off limits for an allium allergy. The chili flake also adds a little heat, a heads up for spice-sensitive guests.

items.name: Marcona Almonds
items.desc: rosemary olive oil, fried rosemary, maldon sea salt
items.story: Imported Marcona almonds from Spain's Mediterranean coast, roasted until golden, tossed in rosemary olive oil and Maldon sea salt, then finished with crisp fried rosemary. Rounder and softer than a California almond, with a buttery sweetness that makes them genuinely hard to stop eating.

ingredients.note: A Spanish almond variety grown along the Mediterranean coast — Alicante, Valencia, and Tarragona. Rounder and plumper than California almonds, with a higher oil content and a naturally sweet, buttery flavor. Spain is the primary producer.
Flaky finishing salt from Essex, England — same as on the bread. Tossed on with the rosemary oil after roasting so the crunch stays distinct.

items.name: Farinata
items.desc: chickpea flatbread, house cagliata, seasonal preserve, fresh thyme, sea salt
items.story: A Ligurian chickpea flatbread with roots in 13th-century Genoa — thin, crisp at the edges, soft and nutty in the center. Made in-house from chickpea flour, rosemary olive oil, and water, finished with fresh thyme and sea salt. The housemade cagliatta and a seasonal preserve sit alongside on the plate. Current preserve: spiced apple butter from Swan House Farm apples.

ingredients.note: Ancient Ligurian flatbread made from chickpea flour, water, olive oil, and salt — baked in a very hot cast iron pan until the edges are crisp and the center is custardy. Also called cecìna in Tuscany. Naturally gluten-free.

Our housemade fresh cheese — whole milk curdled with lemon juice, then dressed with rosemary-infused olive oil and salt. A fresh, mild, milky curd; closer to a soft ricotta than a mozzarella. Made in-house.

The seasonal preserve this fall: Swan House Farm apples cooked down slowly with warm spices until thick and dark. Sweet against the salty cagliatta. Spice mix not confirmed with the kitchen; no nuts or dairy in it.

items.allergenNote: Naturally gluten-free — chickpea flour, no wheat. The cagliatta is plated alongside; for dairy-free it moves to a bowl on the side or comes off entirely, and the preserve stays.

items.name: House Caesar
items.desc: anchovy, parmigiano reggiano, red wine croutons
items.story: Romaine dressed with a classic from-scratch Caesar dressing — champagne vinegar, anchovy, garlic, Parmigiano-Reggiano, egg yolk, Worcestershire, Dijon, black pepper. Topped with boquerones white anchovies and red wine croutons: bread soaked in red wine, butter, garlic, and rosemary, then dehydrated until crisp the whole way through. A clean, honest Caesar.

ingredients.note: White anchovies cured in vinegar rather than salt — mild, tender, and bright. Distinct from the oil-packed brown anchovies in the dressing; these sit on top as a finishing garnish.
Aged Italian hard cheese from the Parma region, with PDO protection. Used both in the dressing (grated) and shaved over the top. Nutty, salty, and complex.
Made in-house: bread soaked in a red wine, butter, garlic, and rosemary mixture, then dehydrated until crisp all the way through. Deeply savory, and the crunch holds up in the dressing.

The dressing is built with egg yolk — emulsified raw with oil and champagne vinegar for a thick, rich, classic Caesar consistency. Not cooked through, similar to mayonnaise. It also carries the anchovy: for fish allergies the dressing has to go, not just the boquerones on top.

items.allergenNote: Every flag has a path, but fish takes two cuts: the dressing itself has anchovy in it, so pulling the boquerones alone doesn't clear it — omit the boquerones AND swap the dressing for oil and vinegar. Croutons on the side handles gluten. The same oil-and-vinegar swap with cheese on the side covers dairy, egg, and allium. Fully modified it becomes a clean romaine salad with oil and vinegar; tell the guest what they're getting.

items.name: Farm House Salad
items.desc: mixed greens, apple, shaved fennel, bread and butter pickled onion, candied almonds, apple vinaigrette
items.story: Mixed baby lettuces with shaved fennel and fresh apple, brightened by crisp bread and butter pickled onions. Candied slivered almonds add sweetness and crunch, and an apple vinaigrette ties the fruit through the dressing.

ingredients.note: A sweet-and-tangy pickle style — onions cured in a vinegar brine with sugar and spice. Despite the name there's no bread or butter; it refers to the classic sweet pickle profile. Bright and sharp against the greens.
The crisp anise-scented bulb, shaved thin and raw. Adds a clean, fresh crunch. No allergens of its own.

Our candied almonds are slivered almonds tossed with powdered sugar and salt — nothing else, so no dairy or egg. Sweet and crisp, a textural contrast in the salad. Guests with tree nut allergies need to know these are here.

Apple cider vinegar and lemon juice blended with green peppercorn, mustard, and shallot, emulsified with canola oil and stabilized with xanthan gum. Carries allium from the shallot, and mustard — which we do not track as a chip, so mention it for a mustard allergy.

items.allergenNote: Tree nuts: the candied almonds come off cleanly for a nut allergy. Allium: the pickled onion and the shallot in the vinaigrette run through the salad, not removable. The vinaigrette also carries mustard, which we do not track as a chip — flag it for a mustard allergy. The candied almonds are just slivered almonds, powdered sugar, and salt — no dairy or egg.

items.name: Burrata
items.desc: roasted persimmon, speck, frisée, pomegranate molasses, saba, crostini
items.story: Burrata served with roasted persimmon, sliced speck and frisée, dressed with pomegranate molasses and saba, with crostini on the side. Creamy, sweet, smoky and salty, with a bitter edge from the frisée.

ingredients.note: A fresh cow's-milk cheese from Puglia: a mozzarella shell holding a center of stracciatella (cheese curds) and cream. Cut into it and the middle should flow.
A fall fruit, honey-sweet when ripe. Roasting softens it and deepens the sweetness against the cheese.
Cured, lightly smoked pork leg from Alto Adige in northern Italy, sliced thin. Pork: not vegetarian, and flag it for guests who avoid pork.
Curly endive. Crisp and pleasantly bitter, it cuts the richness of the burrata.
Pomegranate juice cooked down to a thick, tart-sweet syrup.
Cooked-down grape must from Emilia-Romagna, the unaged cousin of balsamic: thick, sweet, a little tart. Just grapes, no allergens of its own.
Toasted slices of bread for spreading the burrata. Gluten.

items.allergenNote: Dairy: the burrata is the dish, not removable. Gluten: the crostini. Allergens confirmed by Chris 11/13. Contains pork (speck), so not vegetarian as built. The saba is just cooked grape must.

items.name: Ribollita
items.desc: corona beans, cabbage, zucchini, torn croutons, pistachio, chili flake
items.story: Tuscan vegetable soup built on corona beans and cabbage with zucchini. Topped with torn croutons and toasted pistachio. Lightly spicy from chili flake. Fully vegan.

ingredients.note: A classic Tuscan 'reboiled' soup, traditionally a hearty bean-and-vegetable soup thickened with bread. This version is built on corona beans and cabbage and topped with torn croutons.
Large, creamy white Italian heirloom beans, mild and starchy. They give the soup its body.
Toasted pistachio is worked through the dish for richness and crunch. It is a tree nut and, per the kitchen, cannot be removed.

Ribollita's base is built by sweating garlic, bay leaf, red chili flake, and black pepper slowly in extra virgin olive oil, then adding tomato purée and vegetable stock. Once the beans cook, we add sautéed zucchini, carrots, onion, and celery, finishing with diced cabbage and kale. Contains garlic and allium (onion and celery).
This ribollita is fully vegan throughout. The croutons are made without butter and the stock contains no meat, so a guest avoiding animal products can eat the whole bowl with confidence.

items.allergenNote: Tree nuts: the toasted pistachio is integral and, per the kitchen, cannot be removed. Gluten: the torn croutons are a topping and come off cleanly. Allium: the base is built on garlic, with onion and celery in the vegetables, so this dish cannot be cleared for an allium allergy. Fully vegan: the croutons are made without butter and the stock is vegetable, so no dairy or egg.

items.name: Swan House Bolognese
items.desc: saffron spaghetti, pork, beef, rosemary, fennel, tomato, parmigiano reggiano
items.story: The family recipe — on the menu since day one, and it never leaves. This run is built on ground beef and pork raised at Swan House Farm; when it's gone, the dish returns to the classic pork-and-veal build. Either way: seasoned with our own spice blend, cooked down slowly with red wine, tomato, fennel, and rosemary, then finished with cream, butter, sherry, and salt. The saffron spaghetti is extruded with a strained, highly concentrated saffron tea in place of water — that's where the gold color and the subtle earthy aroma come from, no egg involved.

ingredients.note: a slow-cooked meat ragù from Bologna in Emilia-Romagna — traditionally more meat than tomato.

the dried stigma of the crocus flower, hand-harvested and prized. We brew it into a concentrated tea, strain it, and use it in place of water in the extruded dough — gold color, hay-like earthiness, and the reason this golden pasta has no egg.
the aged hard cheese from Emilia-Romagna, the only 'real' Parmesan; nutty, savory, crystalline.

items.allergenNote: No egg in the saffron spaghetti. Dairy: the kitchen can finish it without cream, butter, or Parmigiano — a leaner, brighter ragù. Built in and non-negotiable: allium, the cooked red wine, chili flake, and black pepper.

items.name: Ditalini
items.desc: chickpeas, rosemary, chili flake, sherry vinegar, pecorino romano
items.story: Chickpeas stewed in savory vegetable broth with roasted tomato paste, rosemary, garlic, red chili flake, extra-virgin olive oil and white wine until tender. Half the mixture is puréed for body, then ditalini is folded in with butter and sherry vinegar. Topped with pecorino Romano and cracked black pepper. Thick, savory and warming, with a little heat and a hit of vinegar.

ingredients.note: "Little thimbles": short, small tubes of pasta, the classic shape for pasta and chickpeas or beans. Gluten.

Chickpeas stewed in vegetable broth with roasted tomato paste, rosemary, garlic, red chili flake, olive oil and white wine. Half is puréed so the sauce is thick and coats the pasta. Vegetable broth, not chicken.
Stirred in with the butter at the end for brightness.
Hard, salty sheep's-milk cheese on top. Dairy.

items.allergenNote: Gluten: the ditalini, built in. Dairy: butter in the sauce and pecorino on top. Allium: garlic in the chickpea base, not removable. Vegetarian as built (vegetable broth). Allergens confirmed by Chris 11/13. The wine is cooked in, but mention it to guests who avoid alcohol entirely.

items.name: Girella
items.desc: ricotta and pumpkin seed filling, sage, aleppo pepper, pumpkin puree, marinated kale
items.story: Back on the menu, now as three small spirals instead of one large one. Egg dough is spread with a filling of ricotta, pumpkin seed, sage and Aleppo chili, rolled into a spiral and sliced. The spirals sit on a pumpkin purée and are finished with massaged, marinated kale, pepitas and pumpkin seed oil. Warm, nutty, a little sweet, with heat from the chili. Chris says this one sits close to the squash risotto in flavor; he plans to change the risotto when he has time next week.

ingredients.note: Italian for a spiral or pinwheel. Hand-made egg pasta rolled around a filling, sliced into rounds and baked or sauced. Golden from the egg dough.
Ricotta mixed with ground pumpkin seed, sage and Aleppo chili. Dairy from the ricotta; the pumpkin seed is a seed, not a tree nut.

Per Chris: pumpkin cooked with mirepoix (onion, carrot, celery) and vegetable stock, seasoned with salt, sugar and vinegar, then puréed. Vegetable stock, not chicken. Carries allium from the mirepoix.
Kale massaged by hand, then marinated in vinegar, maple syrup, olive oil and salt. Garnished over the top with pepitas and pumpkin seed oil.
A fruity, moderate-heat Syrian chili flake. It is in the filling, so the heat cannot be left off this dish.

items.allergenNote: Egg and gluten: the egg dough, built in. Dairy: the ricotta filling, built in. Allium: the mirepoix in the pumpkin purée, so the dish cannot be cleared for an allium allergy. Vegetarian as built (vegetable stock in the purée). Pumpkin seeds and pumpkin seed oil are seeds, not nuts, but mention them to a guest with a seed allergy.

items.name: Chitarra
items.desc: manila clams, white wine, garlic, shallot butter, lemon, parsley
items.story: Manila clams are opened in white wine, and that wine is saved to build the sauce. The clam meat is picked from the shells for ease of eating and tossed with the pasta in the clam wine, garlic, shallot butter, lemon and parsley. Bright, briny, clean.

ingredients.note: Square-edged egg pasta from Abruzzo, named for the guitar-string frame it is traditionally cut on. Egg and gluten.
Small, sweet Pacific clams. Steamed open in white wine; the meat is picked out of the shells, so there are no shells in the bowl. Shellfish.
Butter with shallot, finishing the clam-wine sauce with garlic, lemon and parsley. Dairy and allium.

items.allergenNote: Shellfish: the clams are the dish. Egg and gluten: the chitarra dough. Dairy: the shallot butter. Allium: garlic and shallot in the sauce, not removable. Allergens confirmed by Chris 11/13. The wine is cooked in, but mention it to guests who avoid alcohol entirely.

items.name: Risotto
items.desc: arborio rice with sunchoke purée, roasted beets, pickled mustard, caraway
items.story: Creamy risotto finished with sherry butter and Parmesan, folded with roasted sunchoke purée. Roasted beets and pickled mustard bring acidity and earthiness. Caraway runs through it. Garnished with seeds and fresh dill.

ingredients.note: Short-grain Italian rice that releases starch as it cooks, giving risotto its creamy texture. Par-cooked in batches, finished per plate to order. Naturally gluten-free.

Roasted sunchoke blended with water and caraway seeds into a purée and folded through the rice. Just those three things: no dairy, no allium, no gluten in the purée itself (confirmed by Chris, 10/24).
Brings a sharp, acidic bite against the sunchoke. It carries mustard, which we do not track as a chip — mention it for a mustard allergy.
Butter worked with sherry, used with Parmesan to finish the rice. Dairy, and it carries wine (sherry), which cooks in.
A warm, faintly anise seed spice that runs through the dish.
Toasted seeds and fresh dill scattered on top for crunch and a bright herb note.

items.allergenNote: Naturally gluten-free — Arborio rice, no wheat. Dairy: sherry butter and Parmesan. Allium: confirmed in the build, not removable. The pickled mustard carries mustard, which we do not track as a chip — flag it for a mustard allergy. The sunchoke purée is water, sunchoke and caraway only.

items.name: Cioppino
items.desc: roasted cod, manila clams, potato, peppers, fennel · cioppino soup base, white wine reduction
items.story: Pan-roasted cod with ten manila clams. Garlic, shallot, fennel, and peppers go in the pan with white wine and cioppino soup base, reduced down as the clams open. Finished with salt, lemon, and butter. Fennel frond on top.

ingredients.note: An Italian-American fish stew that began with San Francisco's Italian fishermen — whatever came off the boat, simmered in a tomato-and-wine broth. Ours is cod and Manila clams in a reduced white wine and soup-base broth.
Small, sweet Pacific clams farmed in Puget Sound. Ten per plate, simmered in the sauce until the shells pop open, which is how the kitchen knows they are done. Shellfish.
A 7 oz portion, pan-roasted for a crust, then served in the broth. Fish.

The base of the broth. Its full composition has not been specified by the kitchen — confirm the ingredients before clearing the dish for any allergy, shellfish and fish especially, and it may also carry gluten.

Garlic, shallot, fennel and peppers in the pan, deglazed with white wine and the soup base, reduced as the clams open, then finished with butter, salt and lemon. The garlic and shallot cannot come out. The wine cooks in, but mention it to guests who avoid alcohol entirely.
The feathery green tops of the fennel plant, laid on at the end. A light anise note against the broth.

items.allergenNote: Fish: the cod, the center of the dish. Shellfish: the Manila clams, and likely the soup base (composition unconfirmed). Dairy: finished with butter. Allium: garlic and shallot in the pan, not removable. The soup base's full composition is not confirmed, so it could carry gluten or other allergens — confirm with the kitchen before clearing any allergy. Chapeno soup base composition not specified. Confirm with kitchen before clearing for any allergy, shellfish and fish especially: Onion, carrot, fennel, thyme, bay leaf, red chili flakes, black pepper, wine, clam stock, fish stock, tomato paste

items.name: Braised Short Rib
items.desc: sour cream polenta, chanterelle, herbs, horseradish vinaigrette, demi glace
items.story: Beef short rib braised low and slow until it pulls apart with a fork, served over sour cream polenta with sautéed chanterelles and fresh herbs. A sharp horseradish vinaigrette cuts the richness, and a demi-glace ties it together. The heaviest plate on the menu and the one for a cold night.

ingredients.note: A cut from the beef chuck and plate, heavily marbled with lots of connective tissue. Braising (searing, then cooking slowly in liquid for hours) melts that tissue into gelatin, which is what makes the meat rich and spoon-tender.
Ground cornmeal cooked until thick and creamy, finished with sour cream for tang. The house polenta is built with cream, stock and butter, so treat it as dairy.
A wild golden mushroom, firm with a mild apricot-and-pepper note. Fall is peak season in the Northwest. Sautéed here.
White wine vinegar, garlic, shallot, mustard, horseradish, salt, pepper, canola oil
Stock reduced until glossy, thick and deeply savory. Coats the meat as a sauce. Full composition to be confirmed with the kitchen.
Onion and garlic are cooked into the braise with red wine reduced down, so allium runs through the short rib and its sauce. It cannot come out of this dish.

The braised short rib itself contains no gluten. We don't dredge the rib in flour, and our demi-glace is made without soy or wheat. The entire dish is gluten-free, including the polenta, chanterelles, horseradish vinaigrette, and herbs.

Dairy-free works here. The kitchen swaps the sour cream polenta for a dairy-free risotto or builds the plate on a bigger warm chanterelle salad (parsley, chives, shaved shallot). Flag it on the ticket so they build the right base.

items.allergenNote: Dairy: the sour cream polenta is built with sour cream, cream and butter; ask the kitchen whether a dairy-free starch swap works here as it does with the duck.

food.intro: The egg rule for our pastas, before you get asked: every pasta is made in-house, and the dough tells you everything. Extruded shapes — pushed through a die — are semolina and water, no egg. Hand-made shapes — rolled ribbons like tagliatelle, filled agnolotti, gnocchi — are egg doughs. Rule of thumb: if the shape doesn't seem possible to roll by hand (creste di gallo, bucatini, spaghetti), it's probably extruded. But some shapes that are usually hand-rolled, like linguine or chitarra, can be extruded too — confirm with the chef before assuming. Color helps: egg pasta runs golden and silky, extruded runs pale straw. One trap, though — the bolognese's saffron spaghetti is golden from saffron tea, not egg.

desserts.name: Classic Tiramisu
desserts.desc: mascarpone, ladyfingers, planteray rum, caffè umbria decaf coffee, cocoa powder
desserts.story: The classic, built the way it is meant to be: ladyfingers soaked in Caffè Umbria decaf, layered with mascarpone cream spiked with Planteray rum, finished with cocoa. Decaf on purpose, so a late table can order it without a sleepless night.

ingredients.note: Classic Northern Italian dessert — ladyfinger biscuits soaked in liquid, layered with sweetened mascarpone cream, finished with cocoa. The name means "pick me up" in Italian.
Italian triple-cream fresh cheese from Lombardy — thick, rich, mildly sweet. The base of the tiramisu cream layer.

Formerly Plantation Rum — rebranded to Planteray in 2024. French-Caribbean aged rum from Maison Ferrand, known for its dual aging: first in the tropics, then finished in cognac barrels in France. Rich, smooth, and molasses-forward.
Seattle roaster with Italian roots, Pioneer Square. We use their decaf for the soak, so the dessert tastes fully of coffee without the caffeine. Decaf is not caffeine-free; a trace remains.

desserts.allergenNote: Dairy: the mascarpone cream. Gluten: the ladyfingers. Egg: in the ladyfingers, and in the cream if the kitchen builds it on yolks, so treat it as egg either way. The rum goes into the cream uncooked, so there is alcohol in it.

desserts.name: Lemon Olive Oil Cake
desserts.desc: olio verde, apple mascarpone, lemon syrup, brown butter powdered sugar
desserts.story: A Ligurian-style cake where the fat is olive oil instead of butter, which keeps the crumb moist and a little savory. Early-harvest olio verde gives it a green, peppery edge against the lemon syrup. Served with apple mascarpone and dusted with brown butter powdered sugar.

ingredients.note: Early-harvest extra virgin olive oil, pressed while the olives are still green. Grassy, peppery, bright. It is the fat in the cake, in place of butter.
Mascarpone, the Lombard triple-cream fresh cheese, folded with apple. Served alongside the cake.
Butter cooked until the milk solids toast and go nutty, then worked into powdered sugar and dusted over the top. It carries dairy even though the cake itself is made with olive oil.

desserts.allergenNote: Dairy: the apple mascarpone and the brown butter sugar on top; the cake itself is olive oil, not butter. Gluten: wheat flour. Egg: in the batter. No nuts anywhere on the plate. Dairy-free: The dish cannot be done dairy free

desserts.name: Seasonal Gelato
desserts.desc: ask the kitchen for tonight's flavor
desserts.allergenNote: Flavors rotate nightly — confirm eggs or nuts with the kitchen before promising anything.

specials.name: Farmhouse Primavera
specials.desc: rigatoni, eggplant, bell peppers, heirloom tomatoes, pecorino romano
specials.story: Eggplant, bell peppers, and heirloom tomatoes from the farm are sautéed with garlic, shallot, and red chili flake. Tossed with rigatoni in pomodoro sauce, finished with pecorino Romano and tomato leaf oil.

ingredients.note: A wide, ridged tube pasta that holds a chunky sauce well. Standard durum-wheat pasta, so it carries gluten.
A hard, salty sheep's-milk cheese, grated as a finish. Carries dairy.

Our pomodoro is a simple tomato sauce built on garlic and onion — garlic, onion, tomato, nothing else. It's the base for the dish, so the eggplant and peppers cook into it. No cream, no meat, no herbs beyond what's in the sauce itself. Carries allium from the garlic and onion.

Made in-house by blending tomato leaves into neutral canola oil and straining it clear, capturing the grassy, green flavor of the plant itself rather than the fruit. Just leaves and oil — no allergens of its own.

specials.allergenNote: Gluten: the rigatoni, built in. Dairy: pecorino Romano is a finishing cheese and can be left off on request. Allium: garlic and onion are in the pomodoro base, and garlic and shallot are cooked into the sauté — it runs through the dish and can't come out. The tomato leaf oil is just tomato leaves and canola oil, no allergens of its own.

specials.name: Salmon Collar
specials.desc: grilled salmon collar with herb and shallot salad
specials.story: Salmon collar brushed with a calabrian chili paste and grilled to medium. Served with a fresh herb and shallot salad.

ingredients.note: The fatty cut just behind the gills and fins, prized for its rich, tender meat and crisp skin. Grilled here to medium. Carries fish.
Just Calabrian chilies, blended — nothing else in the paste. Chilies from Calabria in southern Italy with a fruity, smoky heat. No allium in the paste; the shallot in the salad is this dish's allium.
A fresh salad of herbs dressed with shallot alongside the fish. Carries allium from the shallot.

specials.allergenNote: Fish: salmon collar, central to the dish and not removable. Allium: the shallot in the salad — the salad can be left off or served without shallot on request, confirm with the kitchen. The chili paste is just blended Calabrian chilies, no allium in it.
